messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered: hosted-api-prod experiencing elevated TLS handshake failures (>= 28% over 5m). Paging primary oncall.
pagerduty: miguel-oncall acknowledged the page — I'm on it
miguel-oncall: collecting initial signals. Who can share customer impact counts? @alex-support
alex-support: ~35 active customer sessions affected, mostly long-poll/streaming. Errors in consumer logs: 'tls: internal error during handshake' and 'remote error: protocol_version'.
sara.sre: jumping in. pulling LB + envoy + app logs. Any recent infra changes or cert ops in the last hour?
jess-prod: cert-rotation CI job executed at 11:50 UTC for hosted-api-prod; rotated cert chain to add a cross-signed intermediate. All health checks passed at 11:54.
ken.net: noticed a route-table adjustment at 11:58 that switched some ingress through a transit path between prod-app-vpc and infra-services-vpc. Looking now for MTU differences.
miguel-oncall: timeline so far: 11:50 cert rotation, 11:55 small error uptick, 11:58 route change, 12:05 significant spike. Rolling timeline docs.
sara.sre: app logs show repeated ClientHello truncation and TLS alert messages. Example:
```
2026-03-15T12:06:13Z app[web.3]: tls: handshake failure from 10.20.3.72: tls: client hello malformed
2026-03-15T12:06:13Z app[web.3]: alert: 40 (handshake_failure)
```
nina-ops: tcpdump from host inside prod-app-vpc shows fragmented ClientHello fragments around 1500-1600B and icmp unreachable filtered on path to certain client IPs.
```
12:05:59.987 IP 10.10.2.4.51234 > 10.200.1.10.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1602, ack 1, win 64240, length 1601
12:05:59.987 IP frag 1: iplen 1613 > MTU
12:06:00.001 repeated retransmit
```
miguel-oncall: ran openssl s_client from multiple AZs: internal AZs connect fine, tests from an EC2 in a different AZ via transit path show immediate TLS decode error. External public curl shows intermittent failures depending on network.
jess-prod: cert introspection: new chain adds ~800 bytes to the ClientHello for certain clients (SNI + alt-svc + OCSP stapling sizes). That increases typical ClientHello size past 1500 in some clients.
sara.sre: hypothesis tracker:
- H1: bad cert chain or cert format post-rotation causing certain clients to reject (x509 verification)
- H2: ALB / envoy listener mismatch selecting wrong cert for some SNI combos
- H3: PMTU/MTU reduction on new transit path causing ClientHello fragmentation -> handshake fail
- H4: VPC peering route instability causing resets mid-handshake

miguel-oncall: testing H1: openssl verify & s_client from inside primary AZ shows full chain valid. Not reproduced there.
jess-prod: rolled cert checks across all targets, no node reported outdated certs. CI logs indicate rotation completed without error.
ken.net: checking MTU: direct peering path MTU=1500, transit-gw path MTU=1438. Transit path blocks ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages, so PMTU discovery stalls.
miguel-oncall: reproducer: from host using transit path, sending a 1600B ClientHello leads to fragment + loss -> server aborts. From host with MSS clamp / iptables adjusting MSS to 1400, handshake succeeds.
sara.sre: mitigation plan (short term):
- M1: revert route change to avoid transit path where possible (Ken)
- M2: enable MSS clamp on ALB/ingress hosts to force smaller TCP MSS (Miguel to canary then apply cluster-wide)
- M3: communicate to support & customers: partial degradation for some networks (Alex)
- M4: keep cert rotation paused for additional canaries until we finish PMTU audit (Jess)

ken.net: initiating route_table revert now. AWS change started. ETA ~4m. tagging with incident id.
devops-bot: Route table revert submitted: rtb-zzz789 by ken.net
miguel-oncall: applying MSS clamp on a single canary node with:
```
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --sport 443 -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400
systemctl restart envoy
```
Canary tests: success — curl from previous failing host completes TLS handshake.
alex-support: first customers confirming recovery on their corporate VPNs. Still seeing a handful of fail reports.
sara.sre: monitoring graphs: TLS handshake error rate falling from 30% to 6% in 10 minutes. Good sign, but not fully resolved.
jess-prod: will run a targeted cert-chain size audit and produce a plan to reduce ClientHello expansion (disable unnecessary SNI ext or trim stapling size) where feasible.
ken.net: route revert completed; BGP/propagation not relevant but AWS reports routes restored to direct peering.
miguel-oncall: rolling MSS fix cluster-wide for now. Note this has some risk with PMTU for legitimate large payloads; we will revert after long-term fix.
nina-ops: uploading packet captures and annotated tcpdumps to incident artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/2470001112/pcaps.tar.gz
alex-support: drafting customer notification to affected customers and internal exec summary.
sara.sre: preliminary root cause (working): the combination of cert rotation that increased the ClientHello size and a recent routing change that sent a subset of traffic through a transit path with a reduced MTU and ICMP blocked. PMTU discovery failed so ClientHello packets were fragmented and lost, causing TLS handshake failures in certain client stacks.

Action items for RCA thread:
- A1: map impacted client IP ranges and identify which networks block ICMP (ken.net)
- A2: add explicit PMTU tests to release pipeline and canary network tests for cert rotations (jess-prod / eng-releases)
- A3: evaluate permanent LB-level MSS clamp or TCP proxy that reassembles fragment-prone handshakes (miguel-oncall / eng-runtime)
- A4: update runbook and add a quick play for TLS/PMTU incidents (sara.sre)
- A5: customer credits & follow-up comms (alex-support)

jess-prod: note: we added the extra intermediate to support legacy clients; we'll explore keeping a short chain for the primary endpoint and an alternate endpoint for legacy compatibility.
miguel-oncall: handing off to sara.sre for RCA writeup and timeline consolidation. I'll stay on-call for the follow-up mitigation implementation.
sara.sre: taking ownership of post-incident RCA. I'll post a formal writeup with timeline, packet captures, and config diffs to #postmortems tomorrow. Thanks for the quick response everyone :thumbsup:
pagerduty: incident acknowledged resolved by miguel-oncall and closed the oncall page
incident-bot: Incident resolved — monitoring stable for 50m. Follow-up ticket created in tracker: INF-5921 for permanent fix.
